title: Primary Function of the System
learningObjectives: Identify the roles of the lever and axial wires.
student: What is the primary structural function of the lever-wire mechanism?
instructor: The hand-operated rigid lever transfers an applied handle force into tensile forces in two vertical steel wires anchored to the base.
gradingNotes: Students should identify the lever as a load-transfer component and the wires as axial tension members.

title: External Load
learningObjectives: Relate the perpendicular handle force to its moment about E.
student: Where is the external load applied, and what mechanical effect does it have on the lever?
instructor: Force P acts perpendicular to the handle at moment arm Lh. It creates a moment PLh about E that is opposed by moments from the two wire tensions.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Identify the constraints imposed by the pivot and wire anchors.
student: Locate the supports and constraints, and state what each restrains.
instructor: Pivot E restrains translation but permits lever rotation. Anchors B and D fix the lower wire ends. Wires AB and CD carry axial tension only.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace force through the lever, wires, and supports.
student: Trace the load path from the operator's force to the fixed supports.
instructor: The handle force acts on the rigid lever; the lever transfers load to A and C; wires AB and CD carry tension to anchors B and D; and the anchors transfer load to the base. Pivot E supplies the remaining force reactions required by equilibrium.

title: Critical Components
learningObjectives: Distinguish deformable components from the rigid compatibility member.
student: Which components are most important for the base mechanics analysis?
instructor: Wires AB and CD are the critical deformable components. The rigid lever controls their displacement compatibility through rotation about E. The pivot is important for equilibrium, but pivot deformation is neglected.

title: Relevant Mechanical Responses
learningObjectives: Identify the responses needed for an elastic-perfectly plastic wire analysis.
student: Identify the mechanical responses that must be evaluated and explain why each matters.
instructor: Determine tension and elongation in each wire, then compare the elastic trial forces with the yield force. If a trial force exceeds yield, the force must be capped under the elastic-perfectly plastic model and equilibrium solved again.

title: Relevant Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify inputs controlling equilibrium, compatibility, stiffness, and yield.
student: Identify the loading, geometric, and material parameters needed for the analysis.
instructor: The required parameters are P, xAE, xCE, Lh, wire length Lw, wire diameter dw, modulus Es, and yield stress σy. Angle θ describes handle orientation but does not enter the moment because P is specified perpendicular to the handle.

title: Student-Generated Structural Idealization
learningObjectives: Convert the mechanism into a rigid body connected to two axial members.
student: Before using the reference figure, draw a simplified Mechanics of Materials model showing the rigid lever, pivot E, two vertical wires, lower anchors, perpendicular handle force, and relevant dimensions.
instructor: A correct model treats the lever as a rigid body pinned at E and wires AB and CD as vertical axial tension members connected to fixed lower anchors. Distances from E must be preserved.
gradingNotes: Students should attempt the free-body and displacement model before seeing the instructor idealization.

title: Modeling Assumptions
learningObjectives: State assumptions supporting equilibrium and constitutive analysis.
student: State the assumptions used to simplify the real mechanism.
instructor: Assume a rigid lever, frictionless pivot, fixed lower anchors, small rotation, vertical axial wire force only, identical initial wire length and diameter, linear elasticity before yield, perfectly plastic response after yield, and neglected lever bending, connection flexibility, pin shear, slack, and strain hardening.

title: Mechanics Analysis Plan
learningObjectives: Plan an elastic-trial and plastic-correction solution.
student: Describe the analysis sequence needed to determine final wire forces and elongations.
instructor: Write moment equilibrium about E; relate wire elongations through rigid-body rotation; use elastic force-deformation relations for a trial solution; compare each trial force with yield force; correct the force distribution if yielding occurs; then obtain elongations from the elastic wire and lever compatibility.

title: Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Interpret all supports and loads in the reference model.
student: From the instructor reference diagram, identify the boundary conditions and support constraints.
instructor: Pivot E constrains horizontal and vertical translation but permits rotation. B and D fix the lower wire ends. Wires AB and CD act vertically in tension, and force P acts perpendicular to the handle.

title: Unknown Reactions and Wire Forces
learningObjectives: Identify equilibrium unknowns and the quantities central to the analysis.
student: Identify the unknown reaction components and wire forces.
instructor: The unknowns are pivot reactions Ex and Ey, tension TAB, and tension TCD. The wire tensions are the main Mechanics of Materials quantities. After they are found, the pivot reactions follow from horizontal and vertical force equilibrium using the resolved components of the applied handle force.

title: Moment Equilibrium About E
learningObjectives: Write moment equilibrium without pivot reactions.
student: Write the lever moment-equilibrium equation about E using the assigned variables.
instructor: TABxAE + TCDxCE = PLh. For the assigned values, the applied moment magnitude is {{lever_applied_moment_Nmm}} N·mm.
gradingNotes: Taking moments about E eliminates both pivot reactions.

title: Rigid-Body Compatibility
learningObjectives: Relate wire elongations using rigid-lever rotation.
student: Use small rigid-body rotation of the lever to relate wire elongations.
instructor: Vertical displacement is proportional to distance from E, so δAB/δCD = xAE/xCE = {{lever_compatibility_ratio}}.

title: Elastic Trial Solution
learningObjectives: Combine equilibrium and elastic compatibility to obtain trial wire forces.
student: Assuming both wires remain elastic, determine the trial force in each wire.
instructor: Because the wires have identical L, A, and E, their elastic force ratio equals their elongation ratio. Combining this with moment equilibrium gives TAB,trial = {{lever_trial_T_AB_kN}} kN and TCD,trial = {{lever_trial_T_CD_kN}} kN.

title: Wire Yield Check
learningObjectives: Calculate yield force and evaluate the elastic trial solution.
student: Calculate the wire area and yield force, then determine whether the elastic trial solution is valid.
instructor: Aw = πdw2/4 = {{lever_wire_area_mm2}} mm2. The yield force is Fy = σyAw = {{lever_yield_force_kN}} kN. {{lever_trial_assessment}}

title: Final Elastic-Perfectly Plastic Wire Forces
learningObjectives: Apply the correct material-response regime after the yield check.
student: Using the elastic-perfectly plastic model, determine the final force in each wire and identify the response regime.
instructor:
{{lever_regime}}

Final forces are TAB = {{lever_final_T_AB_kN}} kN and TCD = {{lever_final_T_CD_kN}} kN. The idealized fully plastic moment capacity is {{lever_plastic_moment_capacity_Nmm}} N·mm.
commonMistakes: A yielded elastic-perfectly plastic wire cannot carry force above Fy.

title: Wire Elongations
learningObjectives: Determine compatible elongations and separate elastic and plastic portions.
student: Determine the corresponding elongation of each wire and identify any plastic component.
instructor: Wire AB is {{lever_state_AB}}: δAB = {{lever_delta_AB_mm}} mm, including {{lever_plastic_AB_mm}} mm plastic elongation. Wire CD is {{lever_state_CD}}: δCD = {{lever_delta_CD_mm}} mm, including {{lever_plastic_CD_mm}} mm plastic elongation. The elastic elongation at first yield is {{lever_yield_elongation_mm}} mm.
gradingNotes: Once one wire yields, determine rotation from the wire that remains elastic and use compatibility for the yielded wire.

title: Engineering Assessment and Recommendation
learningObjectives: Make a limited recommendation based on force, deformation, and material regime.
student: Use the mechanics results to make a limited engineering recommendation and identify important omitted checks.
instructor:
{{lever_recommendation}}

Final design also requires lever bending, pivot and anchor strength, wire termination details, fatigue, fracture, slack, strain hardening, large-rotation effects, and cyclic-plasticity checks.
gradingNotes: The recommendation should be tied to the calculated response regime and should not claim full system safety.
